Time’s up. 2020 marked the end of this strategic period and as such presents an opportune time to revisit the four pillars of the WPS Agenda represented in the framework (Strategic Framework, 2011) and the empowerment of women by the United Nations. To that end, this work asks what content analysis can reveal about UN’s support of SCR 1325.

title: DICTION Computer Program Archival Version
description: This data collection contains the DICTION program, a multi-option, high-speed, content-analysis program that retrieves cognitive, affective, and decisional data from speeches, documents, or archival materials. This computer analysis of textual themes by cluster-analysis technique is designed for use with Robert North et al., BRITISH SPEECHES, 1870-1914, AND GERMAN SPEECHES, 1871-1912 (ICPSR 5902). DICTION is used to produce word-frequency dictionaries, to substitute equivalent words into and delete unwanted words from the text, and to count the co-occurrences of pairs of specified keywords in text input. DICTION also includes routines to delete common English suffixes from text words. It is written in Fortran IV for use with the IBM H Compiler (OPT = 2). Datasets: DS1: Dataset

title: DIEV-T: Database of Incidents of Electoral Violence in Turkey
description: DIEV-T was designed to measure electoral violence in Turkey in both local and national elections that have taken place since 1950. The DIEV-T is constructed on the basis of content analysis of news reports for each election. All documented incidents of electoral violence during the month from 30 days before to 30 days after each election is identified.

title: DNA barcoding media coverage in partner nations 2003-2013
description: We searched media databases LexisNexis, Factiva, and Canadian Newsstand for English language articles and limited our search to print and online newspaper coverage. We searched publications in iBOL partner nations from January 2003-Dec 2013; 2003 was the publication year of the first paper formally proposing DNA barcoding as a large-scale, standardized system for specimen identification (Hebert et al. 2003). We designed our search algorithms to capture articles with iterations of “Barcode of Life” or “DNA barcoding” found anywhere in the article. We manually excluded duplicated (identical publications obtained from more than one database) but not syndicated articles (similar/identical articles published in more than one newspaper under one management or derived from a paid service subscription, such as a newswire service), and non-print articles (for example, newswires that were not published). We also excluded a small number of articles in which DNA barcoding referred to activities other than the differentiation of species using a standardized short DNA sequence. For example, we excluded articles in which “DNA barcoding” described methods used to track an individual animal from farm to market. We developed a priori codes foR content analysis of each article based on descriptions of the iBOL Project and DNA barcoding from the iBOL website and other publications, including: article characteristics, iBOL missions and working groups, barcoding science, and genetic resource sharing. A single researcher read each article and assigned it codes. We assessed the reliability of this data collection method by having a second researcher code a subset of the articles (n=183) to estimate inter-rater agreement. Our acceptable level of agreement ranged from 70-99% for each category used in our analysis, and the average agreement was 87%.

title: Data Package for "Social Sustainability Approaches for Software Development: A Systematic Literature Review"
description: This is the Research Data Package showing the Data Synthesis Analysis conducted based on Thematic Analysis. The abstract of the review is: "Social aspects in software sustainability refer to the impact of the software on the broader social and societal context. It includes considerations such as accessibility, equity, inclusion, diversity, and ethical and human values. To achieve software sustainability, developers must adopt practices and tools that support this dimension. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in incorporating social sustainability into the software development process. This literature study investigates approaches to social sustainability that can be integrated into software development. We extracted and analyzed data from 19 studies through thematic syntheses. The results include a list of recommended support tools based on the social aspects and goals for reaching software sustainability. Considering social aspects in software sustainability ensures that the software is not only technically sustainable but also socially responsible."

title: Data Package: The Public Debate and Popular Support for Universal Basic Income in the Netherlands
description: Data Package for dissertation. This survey aims to gauge opinions on the welfare state in the Netherlands, in particular with respect to the universal basic income policy proposal. It includes attitudes on seven themes: rights and obligations in the welfare state, functioning of the welfare state, work and leisure, universal basic income policy, social assistance policy, politics, and respondents’ labour market position.

title: Data file for the paper “Safeguarding Research: A Review of Economics Journals’ Preservation Policies for Published Code and Data Files”
description: For many years, economics researchers have discussed the importance of sharing code and data files to ensure replicability. The discussion, however, rarely includes questions about long-term access to those files. This paper looks in-depth at the code and data policies from top economics journals to understand the guidance provided to researchers regarding data sharing and asks if that guidance supports preservation of code and data files for access and use, long into the future. We used content analysis to review journal policies from 184 economics journals. We discovered that while most journals recommend code and data be released with papers and that a few journals recommend practices consistent with long-term preservation, almost no journals specifically or emphatically consider long-term preservation of those files.

title: Data fo: Reporting requirements of case reports in medical journals
description: 50 journals were selected from the Scopus citation database (the world's largest knowledge base) that published most of case reports and the authors' guideline section on the type and requirements of writing case reports was analyzed by inductive content analysis.
